full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, J: Petitioner, who stated about him to be a human right activist, obtained Rule from the High Court Division in Write petition No. 3015 of 1997 seeking mandamus upon the respondents, Bangladesh, representative by Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, and the Secretary’s of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Social Welfare and Ministry of Women’s and Children’s  Affairs, Inspector General of Police, Police Commissioner Dhaka Metropolitan, Officer-in-Charge, Kotwali Police Station Deputy Commissioner Dhaka and Commissioner Dhaka Division to restore vacant possession of the building and house being place of business and residence at Kandupatti (situated at the central point of Malitola, Nawabur- English Road, Dhaka) to several hundred sex workers who had been evicted there from on May 11 and 12, 1997 in the manner not authorized by law and why they should not be directed to set the law into motion against the person who took the law into their hands in evicting the inmates of Kandupatti and why they should not be directed to provide to the sex workers full security of the Kandupatti so that they may enjoy their fundamental rights as guaranteed under Articles 31, 40 and 43 of the Constitution of the people’s Republic of Bangladesh. 

 3. The Rule was contested by the respondent No.5, Officer-in-charge, Police Station, Kotwali, Dhaka. The said respondent filed affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia that there was no recognized brothel or brothels at Kandupatti that some Sardernis, leader of the sex workers, used to bring sex workers from various places and used to do the sex business by amicable arrangement with the house owners of Kandupatti area, that in course of time because of social pressure of the nearby became reluctant to give their houe to run the sex business and as a result thereof number of sex workers reduced to 50 to 60, that on 6.5.1997 executive Director Mohila Ain Zibi Samity with her associates entered into Kandupatti and recovered minor girls and thereupon Kotwali Police Station Case No. 20 dated 7.5.1997 was started under Section 9 (Ka) of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Ordinance, 1995, that Kotwali Police on 7.5.1997 arrest of Sardines and a Sarder, that after the arrest of Sardernis  the other sex workers who had no license left brother voluntarily that after departure of sex workers from the brothel the local elites, ward commissioner, and others come out with a procession in protest against the re-establishment of the brothel at Kandupatti.
